purpose: The WSL host crashed during stage C on 2026-09-22 at ~09:10 EDT, mid-encode of the leaf-ir-asym tower. Resume trusts every shard whose recorded sha256 still matches, so before relaunching, every written shard on every tower was re-hashed against its manifest record. A shard that kept its length but lost its contents would pass a size check and enter a published benchmark number silently; only a full re-hash rules that out.
_access_note: Reads document-vector shards and their manifests only. No query, qrel or reserved evaluation payload is opened. The reserved four's shards are included because stage A wrote them and that access is closed, so they should be preserved; they are verified here as artifacts, not re-evaluated. Precisely: what the spent access closed is the reserved QUERIES and QRELS, not the public document corpora, so these document shards are re-encodable in principle -- but the transaction is closed and the artifacts are what the result was computed from (Sol review, 2026-09-22, P3; an earlier version called them 'unrepeatable', which was the wrong word).
method: sha256 over each shard_*.npy in work/m13-reserved-enc/*/*/, compared to manifest.json shards[sid].sha256, the hash m8src/pre_encode.py:encode_dataset records at write time and re-checks on every resume.
head: 1575ef7

damage.diagnosis: UNDETERMINED mechanism; crash-consistency loss of the persisted bytes. What is established: the manifest entry and the inode survived while the file's contents did not, across a host crash. Boot logged 'EXT4-fs (sdd): 8 orphan inodes deleted; recovery complete', which is consistent with crash recovery on this filesystem but does NOT specifically establish that ext4 ordered-mode behaviour damaged this pathname (Sol review, 2026-09-22, P3). An earlier version of this receipt asserted that mechanism and overstated the evidence.
damage.remediation: The 0-byte file was deleted so encode_dataset re-encodes the shard and overwrites its manifest entry. Resume would otherwise have refused on the hash mismatch -- it fails safe, but it fails closed.

repair_verified._what_this_shows: The re-encode reproduced the hash recorded before the crash exactly, so the 50,000 vectors are the same vectors. This confirms the crash destroyed the file rather than the encoder producing different output, and re-demonstrates the deterministic encoding stage A established under expandable_segments. Note encode_dataset does NOT itself compare a regenerated shard against its previous hash -- it overwrites the entry -- so this comparison was only possible because the original hash was recorded here before the file was deleted.
repair_verified.independently_confirmed_by: Sol review, 2026-09-22, which re-derived the same hash from the completed file.

damage._why_not: leaf-ir-asym/climate-fever was mid-corpus and had produced no score. No completed corpus, no per-query row and no published value depended on this shard.

towers_state_after_verification.leaf-ir-asym: 11/22 BEIR-15 corpora complete; climate-fever resuming at shard 30 of 109

downtime.cause: UNDETERMINED. The reboot cleared the kernel ring buffer and journald stopped writing before the crash, so no OOM, thermal or driver evidence survives. Recording this as unknown rather than attributing it.
downtime.budget_consequence: The stage-C deadline is a durable wall clock and ran through the outage. 31.99 h of encode budget remained at relaunch against ~3.3 h of leaf work, inside a 49.05 h total remaining.

limitation: This establishes that the surviving shards are byte-identical to what was written and hash-recorded at the time. It does not independently re-derive the vectors, so it cannot detect an error that was present when a shard was first written and hashed.
